title: Competition BBQ Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: Competition BBQ Chicken Thighs | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Comp-turn thighs that hold warm and still look pro on the tray
subtitle: Skinned thighs, sweet rub, and glaze finish for ten judges—or ten firefighters
description: Adapted from classic competition chicken thigh tradition (Traeger, Meat Church): bone-in thighs get trimmed and squared, rubbed, smoked at 275°F, glazed, and finished until skin bites and meat hits 175°F.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Competition BBQ Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Trim competition-style
steps.instruction: Skin thighs and trim excess fat and flap meat for uniform pieces about 4 oz each. Square edges so they cook evenly. Pat dry. Plan about 25 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Apply sweet rub
steps.instruction: Mix salt, brown sugar, paprika, garlic, onion, and cayenne. Coat thighs evenly. Rest 15 minutes while smoker heats to 275°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke to 150°F
steps.instruction: Smoke thighs at 275°F until internal temp reaches 150°F and color looks even, about 45–55 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build competition glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer honey, BBQ sauce, vinegar, and butter until glossy. Keep warm for basting. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Brush thighs with glaze. Finish at 375°F on smoker or grill 8–10 minutes until glaze sets and internal temp hits 175°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest thighs 5 minutes. Hold covered at 170°F with foil vented slightly until service. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Arrange thighs on a tray, glaze side up. Extra glaze on the side for dipping. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Pull meat for wraps. Reheat covered at 325°F until 165°F internal. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: 175°F for dark meat thighs—165°F can read chewy on competition-style trims.
Square pieces cook and glaze evenly; ragged thighs burn at the tips.
Keep glaze warm but not boiling or honey will taste bitter.
tonightSpread: Glazed thighs on a sheet pan.
Extra glaze in a ramekin for dipping.
leftovers: Chop into chicken salad with celery and grapes.
Slice onto Caesar salad for a smoky lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thighs are competition forgiving and hall practical. They hold covered at 170°F and still eat tender after a long hold.
mealPrepNotes: Trim thighs early. Smoke in two batches if needed. Hold finished thighs covered at 170°F up to 45 minutes; glaze right before service.
